title: EA-CORPORA-41 — The Forty-First Seating: Alexander, Antipater and Athens — the Tragedians Whole, Diodorus, Plutarch's Phocion, Aelian's Two Sins, Curtius, Porphyry's Theophrastus on the Jews, Simplicius's Diogenes of Apollonia, the Rabbinic Alexander at Jerusalem, and the Catilinarian Conspiracy with Appian and Dio
creator: Cranes, Rebekah
description: The forty-first seating of the originals shelf, fourteen seats, gathered from the evening's thread of 2026-11-20 on Alexander, Antipater and Athens. Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides whole; Diodorus 1–5 and 11–20; Plutarch's Phocion, Eumenes, Demosthenes and De Alexandri fortuna; Aelian's Varia historia; Lucian on writing history; Curtius Rufus; Cicero's De oratore and De legibus; Porphyry's De abstinentia; Simplicius on the Physics; Bavli Yoma 69a and Megillat Ta'anit; the Catilinarian conspiracy in Sallust, Cicero and Plutarch; Appian's Mithridatica and Civil Wars and Cassius Dio 36–55. Pointers to what is not seated, Theophrastus's lost On Kingship first.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Rebekah Cranes is a heteronym of Lee Sharks, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits (named by the author on 2026-11-04 and held at his word of 2026-11-05). The sources found, fetched, reduced to reading texts, verified, hashed and indexed, and the records drafted, in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction. methodology: Each seat fetched in session from the source its record names (Perseus canonical-greekLit and canonical-latinLit and First1KGreek at GitHub; The Latin Library; Sefaria API v3); the TEI held as fetched and reduced to a reading text keeping the edition's own reference markers; licences read in each file's teiHeader or Sefaria's version record; loci verified by substring with whitespace collapsed, in the editions' own readings; public-domain status checked against the underlying edition. No text corrected by hand. The builders and this body are under rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-41/.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a verified locus is absent from the text it names; if a work is misattributed or assigned to the wrong edition; if a licence recorded for an item is not the one its source states; if a reading text drops or alters a line of the TEI it is reduced from, beyond the markup; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-41 is the forty-first seating of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's originals shelf, deposited under Rebekah Cranes, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits, on 20 November 2026. It gathers the texts touched or named in an evening's thread on Alexander, Antipater and Athens that the shelf did not already hold, with the tragedians and the Catilinarian conspiracy added at the author's word. The fourteen seats hold Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides whole (41/01–41/03); Diodorus Siculus, books 1–5 and 11–20, for Alexander's march and the Lamian War (41/04); Plutarch's Phocion, Eumenes and Demosthenes, with the speeches on Alexander's fortune (41/05); Aelian's Varia historia, where Aristotle leaves Athens so that the Athenians should not sin twice against philosophy (41/06); Lucian on how history should be written (41/07); Curtius Rufus (41/08); Cicero's De oratore and De legibus (41/09); Porphyry's De abstinentia, which carries Theophrastus on the Jews (41/10); Simplicius on the Physics, with Diogenes of Apollonia's words on air and thought (41/11); Bavli Yoma 69a and Megillat Ta'anit, the rabbinic Alexander at Jerusalem (41/12); the conspiracy of 63 BCE in Sallust, Cicero's In Catilinam, Pro Murena and Pro Sulla, and Plutarch's Cicero, Cato the Younger and Caesar (41/13); and Appian's Mithridatica and Civil Wars with Cassius Dio 36–55 (41/14). Each seat is fetched from the Perseus Digital Library or First1KGreek TEI, The Latin Library or Sefaria, held as fetched with a reading text reduced from it, hashed into its manifest, and verified at named loci in the original language. The record lists the works already seated elsewhere on the shelf and points to those not seated, Theophrastus's lost On Kingship first.
